correctness.rationale: After normalization and padding, each positive tail sign pattern corresponds exactly to a subset J with subset weight at most tau. The two-case square-norm calculation proves tau is at least min(b3,b1+b2), forcing four admissible subsets. The only candidates for the fourth/fifth boundary beyond the empty set and the first two singletons are b3, b4, and b1+b2; this yields the iff condition u<=tau<v. Symmetry converts four positive patterns among 32 into two-sided probability 1/4. If tau reaches v, a fifth positive pattern enters, giving at least 5/16. The argument handles zero padding and coefficient ties; finite enumeration is used only as a regression check.

value.rationale: The source already identifies the exact low-dimensional constant but leaves the extremal geometry implicit. A complete equality classification is a natural structural refinement: it tells exactly which low-dimensional Rademacher sums attain the sharp tail probability and reveals a discrete jump to at least 5/16 outside the minimizer region. The condition is scale-, sign-, and permutation-invariant after canonical sorting, and applies to the whole at-most-five class rather than to an arbitrary parameter slice.
